title: The Lottery Ticket
text:
Ivan Dmitritch, a man of modest means who was quite content with his life, sat down on the sofa after supper with the newspaper. His wife Masha asked him to look for the lottery results. She had a ticket.

He found that the series number matched. Before checking the ticket number, he paused, enjoying the suspense. It might be seventy five thousand roubles. The two of them began to imagine.

Ivan pictured an estate in the country, lying in the sun, going abroad. Then he wondered: why should his wife go abroad? She would fuss, complain about trains, spend his money. He looked at her and found her old and plain, smelling of the kitchen. And her relations would come begging, those wretches.

Masha, meanwhile, had her own dreams, and he saw in her eyes that she too would grab the money and keep it from him. Each began to look at the other with hatred.

At last he checked the number. It was wrong. At once the hatred and the hopes vanished. But the room now seemed dark and small, the supper sat heavy, and the two of them were left bitter and sour with each other.
lesson: Sudden wealth, even imagined, can expose resentments that ordinary life keeps quiet. Contentment is easier to lose than to rebuild.
source: Anton Chekhov, The Lottery Ticket (Vyigryshny bilet), 1887
